en: Of course it is.
Max walks past the Zap-O-Matic. His hand finds the dial all by itself. Click.
Photo 1: everyone round the coffee table, the cake cut, Grandma with a fork, Grandpa with flour in his hair. Kalle and Flimmer wave from the Zap-O-Matic. Caption: "The cake was not a lie."
Photo 2: Zeldina measures the living-room wall with Mouldword's wand. Grandma holds the other end. Caption: "The attic would be available."
Photo 3: Archimedes in Grandpa's bathtub, Ramses between two slices of cake, undecided. Hermes comes through the door, too late. Caption: "Eureka. Again."
Photo 4: the goblins sing in the stairwell, holding signs with syllables. Grandpa conducts with the wooden spoon. Caption: "Cuddles-Pudding, hit the dough."
Photo 4: Grimtooth with a bunch of keys inspects Grandpa's oven. He complains to Model 08/15 or, without him, to Pixel. Caption: "Caretakers among themselves."
Photo 5: Max's empty spot on the sofa. Pixel lies on it, one eye open, looking at the door. Caption: "He's getting it."
That's a cliffhanger. I hate cliffhangers, young man.
I hate them almost as much as time travel, and that's saying something.
He fetched the milk. Voluntarily. Without a password.
I need a moment. Or a tin. Ideally both, in that order.
Sorry, Max, but your milk is in another supermarket.
I stood so long under the bridge, counting rules and counting goats …
But today, my friends, today I chose: I'll sing! And nobody falls in the water!
An egg and some flour, a button, a light,
four worlds and a cake, but no milk in sight!
Clause fourteen b: what you borrow, you give back.
Clause one, brand new: you sing your own track!
And whoever's still sitting will stand up tomorrow …
… and geeeet iiiit!
Pressure normal. I'm letting go now. Farewell, door. It was an honour.
Caretaker, madam. Model 08/15. At your service.
That smells like …
Cake. That smells like cake.
Grandpa. What kind of machine is that.
The dragon egg.
The pharaoh's grain.
The Eternal Energy Cell.
And the Golden Remote is …
I've been to four worlds. I put a troll in a footbath, got a pharaoh to make a decision … talked an AI into madness and got a TV boss off his sofa.
For a shopping list.
And the remote? This afternoon you asked me whether I'd seen it.
You said it out loud on Channel 999. And then came the anvil.
And Zappmann? You know him. Long story, you blinked. I've got time.
That's why the travel posters. That's why the box of remotes. And that's why "preheat".
And what's the cake for? What was the whole end of the world for?
You were too lazy to go shopping.
You sent me into four worlds because you didn't want to go to the supermarket.
Grandpa. You could've just asked me to go shopping for you.
… No. Probably not.
Long story, Grandma. About four seasons.
Grandma. These are … from an old lady who knows everything in advance. Happy birthday.
The machine sighs. The lamps go out one by one, the needle drops into the green, the bolt clacks back. Silence.
The wooden spoon falls out of the door and sticks to the floor. The door swings open.
A smell billows out of the machine. Warm, sweet, brown.
Nobody says anything. Zeldina looks at the ceiling as if checking for damp.
The hatch opens. Grandma stands in the opening, handbag on her arm, and sees: smoke, a cake, a princess, a cat, her husband.
Grandma takes a dog biscuit, bites into it, chews. Pixel makes his horrified face.
Konrad.
The train was on time. So there are still miracles after all.
So you're the new one.
The attic would be available.
And you are?
Finally someone who cleans.
Max. You're standing so straight. What on earth happened to you?
Crunchy. Like Mother used to make.
Right. The cake comes downstairs. Everyone comes downstairs. Including the one with the wand and the one made of tin. It's my birthday, and I'm not celebrating it in an attic.
An … oven. A home-made one. With steam pressure and a mixer. Konrad model.
An egg. Free-range.
Flour. Type 405. Fine as dust. That was important, the dust thing.
A battery. AA. For the remote. It lasts forever if you don't use it.
Mine. The one I've been looking for for weeks. Yes.
For a cake, Max. That's something quite different.
I've been inside before. In the Zap-O-Matic. Once. To test it. Through every channel.
On Channel 999 it fell out of my pocket, right into Zappmann's studio. And I didn't want to admit where it was. Least of all in front of the cat.
1977. "Zappi's Dollhouse." I was the crafts uncle. Every Saturday.
In the last episode I demonstrated an oven live. It exploded. Live. With dough. All over Zappi.
Zappmann was never allowed in front of a camera again. And ever since, I only bake in secret. In the attic. With a safety lock.
The red circle. Today. Grandma's birthday.
I forgot it. Until last night. And shopping … the queue at the till, the parking, the people. I had a television that leads into worlds. So.
I was efficient.
If she notices, the world ends. Mine, at least. That was never a lie, Max. None of it was a lie. Just … put rather grandly.
I could have. And what would you have said?
Hildegard. You're early.
Say it.
Bakery. I said so, after World 2, loud and clear, with a sneeze.
But nobody listens to the cat. Nobody ever listens to the cat.
I knew it. Since Channel 42.
The hologram. "Help me, Max." Who leaves an emergency message in a world he's supposedly never been to?
That counts as censorship. I shall complain as soon as I've found out to whom.
That's why "brochures". My pile was right, young man. My pile is always right, and tonight I'm sleeping on it.
They're both telling the truth. It smells of cake and of remorse.
In humans, remorse smells a little of wet dog. But unlike the dog, you can't be cross with it.
I shall never get over this. I've said it once before, and now it counts double.
She ate it. Voluntarily. With relish.
She didn't raise her voice once. That's power, young man, real power.
I shall study her. From a safe distance, on top of the wardrobe.
I'm only looking for a flat.
It's dark. Grandpa, it's got really dark.
Grandpa, what is that?
That's a remote control.
I carried a remote around for a whole world and thought it was an artefact.
What are you saying?
Grandpa, Grandma's downstairs at the door, and we're locked up here with your work.
Okay. Honestly, that sounded a lot like a final boss.
The glass of milk appears, the cow takes a breath, and the screen cracks. The Golden Remote in Max's hand blinks once. Cut to the attic.
Grandpa takes the egg out of the box and solemnly places it in the left socket. Then the flour sack in the right one. The machine swallows both with a clack.
Max hands it over. Glitter, a soft pop: in Grandpa's hand it is grey and worn.
Grandpa flips open the cover on the back, slides in the cell from the workbench, snaps it shut.
Grandpa points the detonator at the receiver and presses. The machine hums into life. Lamps blink, smoke rises, the needle on the pressure gauge creeps to the right.
The doorbell rings downstairs. Twice. A voice calls up from below.
The machine hisses. An iron bolt slides across the floor hatch, a red lamp blinks. The pressure gauge is in the red.
Konrad? It's me. I'm a bit early. The train was on time, imagine that.
Of course it's dark! It's evening! Four worlds in one afternoon, no day can take that!
The work. I built it while you were away. Four times twenty minutes. I'm surprised myself.
The remote! The golden one! You've got it! Give it here. No. Wait. The others first.
One: the dragon egg, unbroken model. Two: the pharaoh's grain, fine-as-dust model.
Three: the Eternal Energy Cell. Four: the Golden Remote. Now.
The detonator. Fully loaded.
Detonator. With buttons.
It's working! It's working! Twelve minutes, and everything will be different!
No. No, no, no. Not now. Not her. Not before it's time!
Dou… pressure overload! Safety lock! The work is protecting itself!
No one stops my dark work! She mustn't find out before it's complete!
No advert. No cow.
I'm missing something, young man, and until a moment ago I didn't know I could miss such a thing.
Egg. Flour. Battery. Remote.
On Channel 999 I said that out loud once, and then came an anvil.
Now I'm saying it again, very quietly. Without an anvil, if you please.
Nothing. Just watch. This is your moment, not mine. I already had mine, with the anvil.
Your grandfather is bellowing, the hatch is blinking, and you're just standing there.
One of you three ought to do something, and my money isn't on the hatch.
The hatch. Look at it, and then touch it. Afterwards we'll at least know what we know.
Use the hatch. It won't open. But you only think about alternatives once you've tried. That's how you are.
There's a princess standing around here with a Dark Lord's wand.
That's no coincidence, young man. On television they call that casting.
Zeldina told you what she uses the wand for. Doors. Landlords. There's a door here.
Talk to Zeldina and ask her about the hatch. She'll prise the bolt open. I'd have done it myself, but I have no thumbs.
Something is growing behind the little window. If the thing stops, the something will want out.
So someone ought to hold the door. Not me, I'm far too fluffy for that kind of thing.
There's a robot here who's been holding doors since he was built. Ask him. Politely. He's Austrian.
No robot here. But in the compulsory pocket there's something that jams and sticks and has never once complained.
Talk to Model 08/15 and let him hold the oven door. He'll say hello to it. Let him.
Jam the wooden spoon in the oven door. It survived a Dark Lord, it'll survive dough.
The machine only listens to what your grandpa had in his hand. Had. Past tense. Where is it now?
Everything people drop ends up under armchairs. Look under the armchair. Then switch to me, I fit under there.
The remote is under the armchair, the cell right at the back. You take the remote, I fetch the cell, you put it in.
I hate it when I have to list work steps.
You've got a remote. There's a receiver over there. For four worlds you've done nothing but point and press.
Your grandpa shouts especially loudly at one button. People always shout at the right one.
Point the detonator at the receiver and press the red button. Stop. Secure the oven door first, or you'll be eating dough. Again.
I'm still thinking. It looks like staring, and it is staring. But with content.
All done. The hatch is about to open. I'd sit down now if I were you. I'm not you. I'm already sitting.
Someone downstairs has a birthday. It's been on the calendar for weeks. Your grandfather managed it anyway. You don't turn up empty-handed. So they say.
Granny's biscuit bag is in the lost-and-found box. I wouldn't call those biscuits. I've smelled them.
Use the lost-and-found box and take the bag with you. The birthday will do the rest. I'll be looking away.
The dragon egg. Warm, heavy, with a scale pattern. Grandpa says it has to stay in one piece. I'm carrying it like a raw egg. Which it is.
An egg. Just an egg. I saved a world for it. It's looking at me like that's normal.
Size M, free-range, dragon. It doesn't say that on it. But it should.
The golden sack of pharaoh's grain. With a seal. It rustles elegantly when I move it.
A whole pharaoh couldn't make up his mind, but he was sure about the grain. I respect this sack.
A sack of flour. The gold was just the packaging. Grandpa calls it marketing.
The Eternal Energy Cell. It hums very quietly. When I hold it to my ear, I can hear the future. It sounds like rain.
It glows in the dark of my bag. My bag has mood lighting now.
A battery. A very, very good battery. I switched off an AI for it, so the remote had better be pleased.
It says "eternal" on the side. I believe it. This battery will outlive us all. And the remote too.
The Golden Remote, without the cell. Grey and light, as if it had just realised it's made of plastic.
The battery compartment at the back is open and empty. It's waiting, a bit like I wait for school to end on Fridays.
An egg. Three minutes, soft, with salt. I'm not saying that as a threat. I'm saying it as a vision.
Flour. You make things with a crust out of it. I told you in Egypt. I'm not saying it again. Oh, I just did.
I've been holding doors since 2077. This one is warm. I'll hold it anyway. Greetings, door.
The hatch is properly locked. I don't open anything that's proper. Greetings.
Zeldina, the hatch. Can you get it open?
The pressure. The needle. As long as that thing's running, the hatch stays shut, whatever we do.
Nothing. He's got nothing in his hands at all. He's just waving empty hands around.
Zeldina, Grandpa, the robot and me. If we get the hatch open now, Grandma comes in and the thing is still running.
Zeldina, Grandpa and me. If we get the hatch open now, Grandma comes in and the thing is still running.
Can you hold the oven door?
The wooden spoon is wedged in the oven door, it sticks, and it holds. I call that a bond.
The tin head's got the door under control. The spoon stays where it is.
Something red is blinking under the armchair, very regularly. Like a notification nobody reads.
Still blinking. An unread message under the armchair, and Grandpa's got notifications switched off.
There. The remo… the detonator. The cover's open. The cell is gone.
Something's glowing back there. Right at the back against the wall. My arm is too short and the chair is too heavy.
Give it here. No, don't lick it. Give it here.
Cell in, lid shut. Detonator. With buttons. Oh no, I already sound like Grandpa.
A completely normal remote: volume up, volume down, channel, mute and a red button at the top. The red one's the same on all of them.
The red button is all worn. That's the case on every remote, because everyone presses red first.
The red button means Stop, Grandpa. On every remote in the world.
Chocolate. That's chocolate. Why is the end of the world made of chocolate.
The wand opens doors, not machines. And Zeldina won't let go of it anyway.
The spoon doesn't fit in the bolt. It just sticks to it, and that helps nobody.
No cell, no power. I know that from my phone, it's basically my whole life.
Give Grandpa the detonator? He's dropped it once already. And he's used it once already. Better not.
Zeldina rams the black wand into the bolt and twists. Sparks. The bolt springs open. The hatch still doesn't budge.
Max points the detonator at the receiver. Four buttons light up. The player chooses.
The machine gets louder. Much louder. The needle trembles.
The machine changes channel. In the oven-door window, the dough is a newsreader for a moment, then dough again.
Grandpa keeps talking, but you can't hear a thing. The machine hums on undisturbed.
Max presses stop. The oven door flies open, and a gush of brown dough splats into Max's face. The door slams shut, the machine hums on, the needle creeps back into the red.
The detonator! Where's the detonator? I had it! I had it when the doorbell rang!
You've got it! Give it to me! No! Don't point it at the work!
Not the red button!
Not louder! It can already hear!
You see! You see what happens when you don't respect my work!
The cell is nothing without the capsule! Nothing! A button with nothing to push it!
Yes! Give it … no. No, I don't even want it. My hands are shaking. You do it.
Then the thing has to stop running. And who tells the thing to stop?
The one with the detonator. Look at your grandpa. What's in his hand?
He's holding an oven door and greeting it. That is the politest robot I know.
Admittedly, I only know two, and the other one tried to vacuum me.
A wooden spoon is holding back the end of the world. Moderwort would have wept.
I'm not weeping. I'm just close to it, and that's the steam.
I fit under there. I don't like saying I fit under anything, it sounds so much like a diet.
Switch to me. And please don't watch while I crawl.
Dust. A sock. A biscuit from 1998. And a glowing cell.
I'll take the cell. The biscuit I'll remember for hard times.
"Milk prices are rising," he said, and "grandfathers continue to forget birthdays".
That was a very short broadcast. But a very clear one.
Remember that button well. We'll need it again later, for every single lecture.
Hold the door first, then stop it. In that order, just like with tins: open first, then eat.
And don't lick that off. Actually, do. Lick it off. Report back to me.
The tuna tin doesn't hold oven doors. It keeps me in a good mood, and that's its only job.
An iron bolt, and a pretty thick one. Oh, how cute.
The bolt's open. But something's pushing against it from inside. Something big. Something soft.
Then stop it. And hold the oven door first. I once saw what a dragon does when you open the door too early.
I lever bolts, not ovens. There are specialists for ovens.
The hatch. An iron bolt as thick as my arm, and a red light laughing at me.
I pulled on the bolt, and the bolt pulled back. It won, and now I've got a dent in my hand.
Locked. Properly locked. That's not a bug, that's a feature, and I hate it.
Grandpa's work: copper pipes, rivets, a pressure gauge in the red and a little round window. All it needs is a health bar.
If that thing has a second phase, I'm running. Final bosses always have a second phase, and it's always worse.
Behind the window something brown is swelling up. It's growing. I don't know if it can see me, and I don't want to know.
The needle is in the red. Red is never good. Except on trainers.
I tapped on the glass, and the needle trembled. Then I stopped tapping. We understand each other now.
Two sockets, both closed. The egg and the flour are in there. Legendary artefacts. Definitely. What else.
A legendary egg and a legendary flour. In my head an old man says: "It's dangerous to go alone."
A little dish antenna. That's where Grandpa pointed the detonator. The remote, I mean. The thing.
The antenna turns a bit when I move. Either it likes me or it wants something from me.
Grandpa. Red face, white hair, screwdriver behind his ear. If that's the final boss, the rest was the tutorial.
He's sweating and smiling at the same time. Grandpa has nothing to hide, apart from roughly everything.
Hands off, he says. I'm not touching it anyway, I'm scared it'll touch back.
The moon. From outside, it must look really cosy up here.
A star's blinking. Probably a satellite watching channel 999 and laughing its head off at us.
Too small for me, too high for Pixel, and way too high up for Grandma anyway. That's not an exit.
The Zap-O-Matic is still on. Channel 999 shows an empty studio and a golden sofa. No thanks.
The sofa on channel 999 is slowly turning towards me. I turn away. I learned that over there.
Time's running, Grandma's coming, and the hatch is shut. It's an episode where someone's hidden the pause button.
Grandpa's lost-and-found box. On top is a bag of dog biscuits. The ones from the future that were still biscuits over there.
The biscuits from the old lady who knows everything in advance. Maybe she also knew what I'd need them for.
Grandpa's lost-and-found box. He really never throws anything away. And these days neither do I, by the looks of it.
On top there's a voucher for "One lawn mowing", from me, from second grade. Grandpa never cashed it in. He just kept it.
Konrad? Why does the whole stairwell smell of burnt sugar?
I'm coming up now. I'm not counting to three. I'm just coming.
The world will become soft! Soft and warm!
Twelve more minutes, and everyone in this house will know my name!
No one leaves this attic until it has risen!
Hands off! That's set to the exact degree! The exact degree!
I always thought he was harmless. For fourteen years.
Fourteen years, young man. I slept on his lap. I showed him my belly.
"Soft and warm." That's either the end of the world or something you could lie on beautifully.
And I honestly don't know which of the two to wish for.
I'd fit under a door. Through iron, sadly not.
I've never tried, and I'm not trying now either. There are limits, and one of them is iron.
Something brown that grows and smells warm. I am hungry and frightened at the same time.
Those are, incidentally, my two favourite feelings. Usually I have them one after the other.
It smells. It doesn't smell like the end of the world.
The end of the world smells of sulphur, every tomcat knows that. This smells of … I'm not saying it.
The television is the only way out up here. And, let it be stressed, also the only way in.
Think about who tends to come in through ways in. Old acquaintances, for example.
The dog biscuits survived the journey. Sadly.
Some things are more eternal than any energy cell, and nearly all of them are inedible.
You're taking the dog biscuits. Now. While your grandmother is coming up the stairs.
I saw nothing. I wasn't here. I am a rumour.
Eureka! No, wait, wrong occasion. A locked attic? A lever! You need a lever!
Max! Kssh! I can't get out, I'm static! But I'm keeping my fingers crossed! I don't have fingers! Kssh!
Locked in? Then you need the Gerd Glück skeleton key, for a limited time only, now with free Gerd!
Greetings, lad. Locked, you say? Properly? Then I'm coming. Order is my speciality.
I'll be back. I said so. I keep my word. I keep hold of anything you hand me.
Supple, lad. Olive oil, cold-pressed. I feel brand new. What shall I hold?
Your ally is in another channel!
Max! Dude! The caretaker is on his way to Konner number 31. I can send you meow-Morse. Does that help?
Thought so. Good luck, man. You've still got the spoon!
A call for help via the TV. I hope someone over there has their notifications on.
Channel 3. Zeldina! We're stuck, Grandpa's lost it and the door's locked!
Zeldina, this is an emergency. Not a viewing.
Channel 7. Archimedes! Ramses! Anyone!
Thanks. Very helpful. All of you.
Channel 42. Hello? Anyone with joints?
No, Kalle. Honestly, no.
Channel 999. Flimmer? Anyone?
Zappmann?
Good. Good for him.
Zeldina, what was that magic wand?
So, was the tower worth it?
How are the joints?
For landlords?
And what are you looking for now?
Zeldina climbs out of the screen, dusts herself off and looks around as if she's at a viewing.
Model 08/15 steps out of the screen, bows with a clank and looks at the machine like a stain that has to go.
Nobody is sitting on the golden sofa. There's a note on it: "Got up. Z."
We need help, and it has to come from over there.
You know people there. I mainly know food there, and food sadly doesn't come when called.
Nowhere yet, Princess. And that is exactly what I find so unsettling.
Had you oiled the tin head, he'd be standing here now.
I don't say that as a reproach. I say it for the record, and the record forgets nothing.
Should I help? Or rather not? I'm thinking it over. I'll get back to you. Maybe. Quite definitely maybe.
Thank you, Max! But the princess is … oh no, there she is.
A locked door, a landlord who's lost it and an attic? I'm coming. That's my core competence.
Sloping ceiling, skylight, period building. Pretty. What are the service charges like?
Everything's a viewing if you look long enough. All right then. Where's the fire?
So. A princess, a cat, a boy and an inventor who's lost it. That was enough in every fairy tale, so it'll be enough here.
So. A princess, a cat, a boy, a caretaker and an inventor who's lost it. That's practically a flatshare.
Mouldword's. He left it behind when he went back to school. I use it for doors that stick. And for landlords.
Seven floors, no lift, a dragon as a lodger. I love it. I'm still looking. You always keep looking.
They stick too. Usually on the deposit.
Something with a lift. And without a dragon. He can come to visit, though, he always brings coal.
A sign. A pretty clear sign, actually.
"Today only." I knew it was coming. It's been written in the stars for four worlds. And on the display stand.
The last quest. No dragons at all.
The milk is right at the back. Of course. Every shop is a dungeon, and the milk is the treasure in the last room.
No static, no channel, just a door that opens by itself. And I'm walking through voluntarily. That's new.
Cut. Supermarket entrance, late in the evening. Max stands in front of the glass door, hands not in his pockets.
The door slides open. Max goes inside. The light from the shop falls onto the pavement. Fade to black.
I'll be back. With the tea towel.
The cake. Lopsided, brown and warm. So that was the final boss, and I just cut it.
The cake is still steaming. It's been through four worlds, a dragon and a final battle. It looks very relaxed for that.
A garland. Grandpa put it up while I was in antiquity, with drawing pins, straight into Grandma's wallpaper.
The garland is crooked. Grandpa says it's on purpose. Grandma says it's Grandpa. They're both right.
Little presents. One of them is a remote control cover. Grandpa's learning, just slowly.
One present is wrapped in newspaper, the TV guide to be exact. I recognise Grandpa's dog-ears.
On every photo Grandma looks like someone's forgotten her birthday. Now I finally know why.
In the newest photo Grandma's smiling. It hasn't even been taken yet, but I already know what it looks like.
The sofa looks smaller than at lunchtime, somehow. Or I've grown. Both fairly unlikely.
The Zap-O-Matic is in the living room now. Grandpa says TV on birthdays is a tradition. Grandma says nothing. That's worse.
The Zap-O-Matic is showing some colourful stripy picture, and Flimmer is waving from the corner. I wave back. Nobody here gets why.
This is where the remote used to lie, and now it's lying here again. The dust outline fits exactly.
I put the remote exactly in its dust outline. Perfect fit. The sofa sighs. So do I.
The caretaker is washing up, without being asked. Grandma watches him like a sunset.
He dries every cup separately and says "Greetings" to each one. Grandma gave him an apron. He's weeping oil.
Page 3. An egg, soft-boiled. Something made of flour. Batteries. Milk.
Pixel. Your shopping list is Grandpa's shopping list.
At the very bottom of page three it also says: "Next year: sofa for two." In Pixel's paw-writing.
Grandma, did you know Grandpa used to be on television?
Grandpa, and the password?
I'll get it.
Later. Milk first. You finish one quest before you start the next.
No, thanks. This is a one-person quest. You stay, Grandma's bound to have more questions about the rent.
I'm off, then. To the supermarket. Voluntarily. And nobody say anything.
Good evening. Happy birthday, Mum.
I'm not asking. I've had a late shift. I'll ask tomorrow, and in detail.
Dad, this is your shopping list. You didn't buy any of it, did you?
Eggs. Flour. Batteries. Find the remote.
And milk. Where's the milk?
The cake is on the coffee table. It's lopsided, steaming and looks magnificent. Grandma cuts the first slice.
The door opens. Max's mother comes in, jacket still on, keys in hand. She sees a robot washing up, a princess with cake, a cat on the cupboard. She takes one deep breath.
She picks a crumpled note up off the coffee table, right next to the remote.
Silence. Pixel lets himself drop from the cupboard towards the sofa. Grandpa pulls a second note out of his cardigan and holds it out to Max. It has something with lots of characters on it.
Max looks at the note. Then he stands up. He doesn't take it.
Pixel misses the sofa and falls off the cupboard onto the carpet in shock.
It's risen. I'll give you that, Konrad. It's risen.
A cake without milk? Konrad.
That's where I met him. I was in the front row when the oven exploded. The dough hit me. I thought: he's the one.
The boy is all right. You're not, Konrad. But the boy is.
He apologised. With a cake. He's baked me one every year since. Usually none of them explode.
Seventy minutes at steam pressure, mixer on setting …
Milk was … milk wasn't on any channel.
In a minute. I wrote it down. It's somewhere I look every day.
The password. A scientist's word of honour. Here.
Max. The password. You didn't even take it.
Milk was on every channel. Five seconds at a time, three times, with a cow.
I was the only one in this house who looked. I don't expect an apology. Actually, I do.
The sofa. My territory. I left it to you humans for a few worlds, out of sheer generosity.
The loan period has now expired.
Zeldina is checking the wallpaper for mould and asking your grandmother about the rent.
And your grandmother is answering her. With figures. I'm a little frightened.
She asked whether the castle had been renovated, and your grandmother said yes.
I believe she meant the bathroom. And I believe nobody will ever clear that up.
I was the only one with a plan the whole time. Feel free to tell people.
Salmon wasn't on it, though, and I shall never forgive the universe for that.
He … He said …
Did anyone record that? Grandpa! Was the camera running? Any camera?
I'm saying something. I'm just saying it later, when I can sit again.
Romantic. With dough. I need to sit down for a moment.

I'll wait here! Or I'll run after you! I can do both!
A bean! A real one! Plant it! Water it! I'll fetch … I have nothing to fetch. I'll fetch my breath.
A beanstalk! She's up there! Definitely up there!
Then she's in another castle. That's what I'll say then. That's what I always say.
Baa.
Baaaa.
Nothing's open right now. Go somewhere you haven't been yet,
or somewhere there's something to eat. Both count, but the second counts more.
The landlord's cat won't let you near the pot. She needs distracting.
Charming distracting. I name no names, but one of them begins with P.
The landlord is stuck to that pot like I am to the radiator. He needs a reason to leave.
One that's as far away as possible. As far down as possible.
Gollo doesn't dare. He wants to play first. Riddle games, what else.
Whoever wants to take that ring off him has to beat him first.
I could talk to Minka, cat to cat, so to speak. Switch to me, if you dare.
Take a look at the wine list. There's something on it that's right at the back of the cellar.
He only loses to a question whose answer only you can know. Something you're carrying, for example.
Switch to me and talk to Minka. I'll lure her out. My charm is a force of nature.
Order the Mount Doomsday vintage. He has to fetch it from the cellar, and that takes a while.
Drag the tin of tuna onto Gollo. Then ask him what's in your pocket. He'll never guess.
The wandmaker says the wand chooses the wizard.
Sounds to me as though the wand needs a good reason to stick to you. A sticky reason.
There's something sticky in the tavern. It bubbles, and I dream about it at night.
Smear cheese on the spoon. I'm a tomcat, not a walkthrough.
The troll wants three goats, and we have none. That is, if I may say so, a poor start.
One goat is eating at the blacksmith's, a second one can be ordered at the village board. The third … please no.
Fetch the forge goat. Order the second with the form from the village board and give me the goatskin rug from the tavern. I hate everything about this.
The troll is a stickler for rules. Read the bridge sign. All of it.
The goats have to say their lines. They only speak Goatish. I'm fluent, by the way.
According to the statutes the troll has to go into the water. He can't swim. Read exactly what it says.
In the fairy tale it's always the little one first, then the middle one, then the big one.
Read out the text from the statutes, I'll translate. Mostly correctly.
It says "water", not "river". There's water in other places too.
Send the goats over the bridge little, middle, big. I'm the little one. Don't tell anyone.
Read out the statutes, then switch to me and talk to the goats. The second time I'll translate properly.
Get water from the well with the bucket and put it in front of the troll. Footbath. Rule fulfilled.
The well wants gold. Toadi only has mushroom money, and you?
What do you actually have in your pockets, apart from crumbs and a phone with no signal?
Gollo's coin belongs in the well. And then don't wish for anything I'd regret.
Coin in, wish for "something that wants to go far". Not pizza. I say that in pain.
Alwin wants egg, milk and a glow mushroom, so a pancake that glows.
Ingredients have to be gathered, young man. They don't come by themselves, I know that from the tuna.
Six bottles, one note. Read the note. Twice.
It rhymes, but it doesn't lie. Unlike certain noses I'd rather not specify.
Egg from the hen in the tavern, mushroom in the enchanted forest, and there's no milk here. Except from animals with bells.
Not at the ends. Not the big ones, they're twins. And the fish oil stands to the right of the potion. Right as you see it.
Take the jug from the forge, milk the goat, throw egg, milk and mushroom into the cauldron. I'll look away.
Bottle three. The third from the left. I'd have said four, and I'd have been lying. Take three.
The roses only open for singing. You don't sing, and I don't sing in public.
So who sings around here in secret?
There's music under the bridge. The troll doesn't just listen to it. Ask him. With the sock in your hand.
Talk to Waldemar about singing, follow him into the forest, hold the sock into the pollen. And promise him the end credits, it costs you nothing.
A bean won't grow in your pocket. It needs soil. There's a patch of soil next to the well. Coincidence? No.
Plant and water. To water it you need the bucket from the well. With water in it, if you dip it in.
Bean in the soil patch, fill the bucket at the well, water on the bean. Then climb. You. I'm being carried.
The estate agent wants commission. Haggling gets you nowhere, pets get you surcharges. She wants to sell something. Give her something to sell.
You've got a wanted poster in your pocket. An estate agent reads that sort of thing as a brochure.
Show the estate agent Mouldword's wanted poster and pitch her the tower. Seven floors, tower location. I will never say anything like that again.
The goblins want light and a signature. Or a career. Grimtooth can be bought, just not with money.
Option one: the glow potion from Hogglewarz is a torch, and ketchup looks like blood. Option two: Zeldina needs a caretaker.
Give Grimtooth the glow potion and sign the agreement in ketchup. Or offer him the caretaker job together with Zeldina. One is enough.
Four parts, one order. Every place you found one tells you what hangs on what. Look in the notebook, not into thin air.
Three brooms, three routes. They sweep anything that moves. Preferably hair. I have hair. I can see where this is going.
Mo is the beginning, says Zeldina. The report card hangs Cuddles on Mo. The song hangs Pudding on Cuddles. And Teddy comes at the end, with dots in front.
Switch to me and find the spots where the tile paths cross. One per route. That's where I shake myself. Under protest.
Mo-Cuddles-Pudding-Teddy. Say it to the door. Never say it to me.
Switch to me and click the three crossings. The brooms run into the storeroom, you shut the door. And you buy me a brush.
Smaugi won't give anything away unless someone really needs it.
And there are three people standing around here who need something rather urgently. Not counting me, I only need fish.
Humbert collects swords, Grimtooth needs torches, Zeldina wants a chandelier. Smaugi's heap has all three.
Swords to Humbert, torches to Grimtooth, chandelier to Zeldina. Then he'll give you the egg. And I want it soft-boiled.
He has no nose, but hay fever. And you have a sock full of pollen.
I'm no mathematician, but even I can work that out.
Sock open, he sneezes, the staff flies. Then he needs a replacement. You have a spoon that used to be cheese.
Sock on Mouldword, wooden spoon on Mouldword, then call him by his pet name. And don't look at me while you do it.
I'm still thinking. Here even thinking has statutes. Clause one: no pushing.
Brooms and cat hair, it always ends up in the broom cupboard.
Ah, a new dropout! Welcome to Hogglewarz! Show me your wand, boy.
No wand? Then come back when something has chosen you. A wand, a spoon, a destiny. We take anything.
A wooden spoon! Finally someone with a sense for the essentials. The exam may begin.
A tomcat! Do you have hair? Of course you have hair. Away from the broom! Away! … Too late.
Brew the Potion of Glowing. The recipe: one egg, one jug of milk, one glow mushroom. And finally the secret ingredient from the shelf.
Is it? Isn't it? The boundaries are fluid. Like batter.
The mushroom. Without the mushroom it's breakfast, with the mushroom it's education. Glow mushrooms grow in the enchanted forest, beyond the troll bridge.
Milk? There's no milk left in the entire kingdom. The Lord takes his coffee black now. Hence the mood.
But goats. Goats have milk, they say. I've never checked.
Six bottles. Someone swapped the labels. Probably me. My note tells you which one is right. In rhyme. I used to be a bard.
A pupil. First year. He sneezed in Herbology, everyone laughed, he left. Very sensitive.
His school report is still in the archive. Never collected.
I laughed too. He sneezed very loudly. I think of him often, mostly when things are in bloom.
Enchanted. All the brooms here are enchanted. They sweep whatever moves. Cat hair moves most beautifully. Don't ask me why.
Off you go. The cauldron won't run away. Well, it did once. Long story.
Not the fish! That would be a quiche!
Three ingredients. Now the last one: one of the six bottles. Choose wisely. Or quickly. Either way you get a story.
Six bottles on my shelf, as anyone can see: one potion and one oil, two poisons, two juices, all plain as can be. My shelf has never managed more, take it from me.

The fish oil that stinks stands just right of the potion, quite near. The two giants are twins, filled up to the brim. And the ends of the shelf never hold what you're after, I fear. That's all of my rhymes, so don't shed a tear.
Wrong bottle. Don't worry, it grows out. Usually upwards.
Passed! The Potion of Glowing! Bottle it, take it, don't drink it. It tastes of pancake, and that's confusing.
And because you passed, I'll show you how not to do it. Mouldword's school report. From the archive. As a deterrent.
His mummy signed it. He never collected it. I think that's exactly why.
The floating one. The milk has a nicer view now than I do.
I could. But then I'd have written the rhyme for nothing. I spent four days on a rhyme for "slime".
Exactly. Nothing decent. On the fourth day I crossed it out again and went to bed.
That's what they all say. The broom doesn't believe anyone.
A broom with a persecution complex. If somebody films that, it'll have a million followers by tomorrow.
Wonky school desks, and I bet there's gum stuck under every one.
There's a heart carved into one desk: "A. + ladle". The headmaster used to sit here himself.
An empty blackboard. Either Alwin has nothing to say, or he's forgotten everything again.
Right down in the corner there is something after all: "Do not wipe!" Everything around it has been wiped.
A cauldron bubbling away with nothing in it. It has nothing to say and keeps saying it anyway.
I had a look inside. There's a noodle stuck to the bottom. Something other than potions has been cooked in here.
Six brown bottles without labels, and two of them are twice as big. That's either magic or marketing.
There are six rings of glue on the shelf. So the labels did exist once, and somebody didn't want them any more.
High windows. Outside there's weather, inside there's a timetable.
A pupil flies past outside, backwards. He waves as if that were the plan.
The headmaster. Star-spangled robe, cooking apron, ladle. He doesn't know himself what he's teaching right now.
A sock full of holes, lying on a stool like a guest of honour.
The holes are round and all the same size. That wasn't moths, that was a spell that missed.
The practice broom's lying in the cupboard, twitching. It's dreaming about cat hair.
There's a tag on the handle: "Practice broom. Does not fly. Only sweeps, and not gladly."
Toadi's standing in the doorway with his fingers crossed, both hands. That's all the fingers he's got.
What do I have to do for the exam?
That's a pancake recipe.
And what turns a pancake into a glowing potion?
Where can I get milk around here?
What's the deal with the shelf?
Who is this Mouldword, anyway?
He left just because everyone laughed?
What's wrong with the broom?
See you later.
Egg in. It bubbles yellow, like every pancake does.
Milk in. The whole jug.
Mushroom in, and now it's glowing. I made a pancake with built-in lighting.
Cheese in, and it turns into a bake. I bet Alwin has rules against that. I think.
Use the spoon for stirring? No, it's a magic wand now, there are expectations stuck to it. And cheese.
Egg, milk and mushroom first. Alwin's strict about that, about the recipe, anyway. Not so much about anything else.
Directly to the right. Hopefully from where I'm standing, or I'm about to become a mushroom.
In it goes.
I'm a mushroom. I feel kind of … grounded.
Bottle three. Not at the edge, not big, and the fish oil's right next to it on the right. Pixel, you lied.
A potion that glows. I still wouldn't drink it. Then I'd glow.
"Herbology: fail. Potions: fail. Malice: satisfactory." And a note: "For my little Mo-Cuddles, so proud!"
A report card with a pet name on it. That's worse than any class photo where you blinked.
Glows in the dark, says so on the label anyway.
I hold my hand over it, and it gets a bit brighter. Good enough for a night light, probably not for a Dark Lord.
I already passed the exam. One more potion and Alwin's going to hire me as a teacher.
Bottom right it says: "Conduct: outstandingly evil." With a gold star. I bet he had that framed.
A bottle with no label. Whether this is brave or stupid, the cauldron's about to decide.
One bottle per go. If I tip two in at once, I bet I won't get a potion, just chaos.
In which castle?
Can't you just tell me which one it is?
So what does rhyme with "slime"?
A small broom in the corner twitches, stands up and races after a tuft of grey cat hair. Crash. Cupboard.
The cauldron flares yellow and lights up the whole classroom.
I'm shedding, that's grooming, not an invitation!
This broom clearly has no upbringing, and I shall complain to its manufacturer.
Six bottles, no labels. I can smell them from here, all six.
But I like to be asked. At least twice, and the second time with more feeling, please.
That one retired after the third year group, because the pupils wore it through.
Someone should give it a cushion. Anyone who has endured that much deserves a cushion.
Chalk, soot and old pancake. This school has history.
Deep-fried history. I can smell at least three hundred years of frying fat, and I am impressed.
You poured all the milk into a cauldron, without a single drop for the cat.
I shall remember that. For life. And cats, as you know, have nine of those.
Nettle. That's how plants smell when they're offended, and this one is very offended.
Mushroom, and bitter. Whoever drinks this will become one.
I just made that up, young man, and I'm still completely certain.
Lemon, honey and a hint of trouble. Could be anything.
I shan't commit. Only dogs do that.
The potion! Definitely! It smells of success and lemon and … the sea.
Success smells of the sea, everyone knows that. My nose vouches for it.
Mushroom poison, just like the other big one. The two giants are twins, and neither of them is nice.
Nettle, at the edge of the shelf. What you're looking for is never there. Even the note knows that, and it's made of paper.
Two bottles, and I'm sniffing no more.
After that my nose goes on holiday.
A mushroom in a hoodie. I'm not taking a photo, because I don't have hands.
That is my only reason. Remember that.
That was the fish oil. I said potion, and my nose said potion.
We both stand by our mistakes, but not loudly, and certainly not in front of witnesses.
Interpreted.
Mo-Cuddles. One writes that down.
One writes it under one's paw and reads it to oneself in difficult hours.
The cauldron bubbles, the bottles are silent, and Alwin is humming a recipe.
You could join in. At least with the humming.
The broom in the cupboard is still twitching, dreaming of my fur.
I feel flattered and threatened at the same time, and that's a rare state for me.
I am not moving. I am decoration, and the finest in this room.
Family?
Cheese fondue in a bowl. It's still bubbling. In my pocket. Which now has an operating temperature.
A wooden cooking spoon. The wandmaker says the wand chooses the wizard. This one chose stew.
I waved it around in the air, but not a single spark came out. I think it needs something to hold it together.
A goatskin rug. It smells of tavern, beer and goat, in exactly that order.
Little Red's order form. One box for "Grandma", one for "Wolf" and one for "Other". I'm Other.
The small print says: "Delivery only to the edge of the forest, beyond that at your own risk." Honest, but pretty creepy.
Mouldword's wanted poster. He looks like someone who was never allowed to smile on class photo day.
"Reward: a kind word." Nobody signed it.
An empty bucket. If I talk into it, it echoes. It's got more echo than my class when the teacher asks a question.
On the bottom it says "Property of the well". I'll take it back, sometime. Promise. Almost a promise.
A bucket full of water that sloshes with every step. I'm walking around like a waiter on black ice.
An empty jug from the smithy. No name tag yet. Humbert mustn't see it.
I said "hello" into it, and it said "hello" back. That's a start, at least.
A jug of goat's milk. Fresh, warm and a little reproachful. The goat was watching.
A chicken egg, still warm. The chicken stared at me for a really long time. I owe it one.
A glow mushroom. I hold it like a torch, and the best part is: it never needs charging.
It glows brighter when I praise it. I said "good mushroom", and it's beaming.
Alwin's hint note. His handwriting slopes upwards, like the note's about to take off.
At the bottom he's drawn a star with a hat. A wizard who draws stars with hats can't be a bad person.
A tiny vial. It barely holds a drop. Sample size.
The label says "Drink me". Not happening, I've read in books what happens next.
Now the vial is big. That went faster than it did for me. And without the voice breaking.
Little Red's ketchup. A tomato is laughing on the label. It doesn't know what happened to its friends.
I squeezed a bit, and it made a rude noise. Little Red really could have warned me.
A collective agreement, still blank. One line for the signature and one for the coffee. The goblins have priorities.
Section one: "Breaks." Section two: "More breaks." Section three is missing. I guess they took a break.
The dragon egg. Smaugi kept it warm, and now I'm carrying it on. I'm officially a babysitter, for an egg.
Melted cheese. It clings to everything it loves.
I'm keeping my distance. I'm not ready for that kind of relationship yet.
A fur without a goat. That's the best form of goat there is.
I shall lie on it as soon as you're not looking. Out of revenge, so to speak.
Water in a bucket. That is a weapon, young man.
I know it, and you know it. We won't talk about it, and you won't point it at me.
Milk. I'm not proud of it, but for this jug I would do things.
Terrible things. Things after which you're no longer allowed on the sofa.
An egg. Three minutes. I'm just saying,
in case you ever need a plan. I always have one, and it always involves food.
A bottle that grows. I'd have preferred a tin that grows,
but nobody asks me. I merely offer it as a suggestion to the manufacturer.
I've looked at it again. It's an egg, a big one.
I stand by my opinion on how to cook it: two and a half minutes, and not a second longer.
Viewing in progress! Three months' rent commission, in dragon gold, or no keys. Next!
A pet. Surcharge. Per hair.
Four. Haggling costs extra. Five if you keep looking at me like that.
A pet? Cat surcharge. Plus hair surcharge. Plus a surcharge for the look he's giving me right now.
Seven floors … tower location … "Wanted". That means: motivated seller.
That's the commission of my life. Viewing postponed! I have to make a Lord an offer!
I'm up top, standing on a cloud. My physics teacher would be crying right now, and rightly so.
The end of the beanstalk. Hopefully going down's easier than coming up.
I looked down, and the village is tiny down there. I'm looking back up now, up is healthier.
A pastel archway, and the castle behind it. Two rooms, cloud view, very airy.
There are clouds carved into the arch, made of cloud.
Child's handwriting in chalk: "…-Teddy was here." The beginning has been wiped off.
Next to it, a little chalk heart and a stick figure with no nose. I know that figure from the wanted poster.
A balcony with a view of everything. That railing has definitely never met a safety inspector.
I'm not leaning on the railing. I've seen how it wobbles when a single cloud drifts past.
Finally, someone who gets me.
Clouds you can walk on. I'd rather not jump. Because of the people below.
I stepped on one, and it squeaked quietly. Like a sofa cushion that's scared of heights.
The estate agent. Hair bun, clipboard and a smile with small print underneath.
She smiles when she says "cloud view". When she says "deposit", she smiles even more.
Short hair, crown tied on with string, moving box under her arm. Kidnapped looks different.
She carries her sword on top of the box. That's not a princess who wants rescuing, that's one who's moving house.
You're the princess?
Toadi is looking for you everywhere.
So were you kidnapped or not?
What about the estate agent?
Yes. … Still.
Later.
Two months' rent?
I could offer a tomcat as a flatmate.
I might have a property for you. Brochure attached.
Dark tower. Seven floors, tower location, owner open to offers soon.
Pixel?
Brokered.
Hang on. If the estate agent talks Mouldword out of his tower … the tower becomes vacant.
What do you know about Mouldword?
What do you want with the tower?
And if Mouldword won't move out?
Do you know the goblins?
Let's go.
And the dragon? The tower? The whole kidnapping thing?
And he never read it?
Four parts? How long is that?
You mean I should offer him a job?
Pixel opens his mouth. Nothing comes out. For the first time ever.
Soft, cool, and it holds. I'm staying here until someone carries me back down.
And just so we're clear: by someone, I mean you.
Teddy. Someone was called Teddy here and survived it.
Barely, only just. Someone once called me "Kitty-Wiggles", and I didn't eat for three days.
Old chalk, and tears. Someone cried while writing this.
With a name like that I'd have done the same in his place. In public.
At last, someone with eyes in his head. We're taking him with us, young man.
No? Then I'll simply come here every day. I don't mind long journeys, as long as I'm carried.
Cardboard, crown polish and determination. This woman smells of a plan.
That's rare. Most people smell of lunch, and I don't mean that as a criticism.
She stroked me without looking, but with great respect.
And with a hand that usually holds crowns. For that, I even forgive her the taped-up boxes.
That is the cleverest person in this world.
I say such things about humans reluctantly, and even more reluctantly out loud.
That's none of our business. We want an egg. Only an egg.
Other people's flat-hunting is the most boring thing I know, and I know rain.
That's not a look. That's my face.
I have composed myself again. That was a shock, a real shock.
I need tuna, immediately. Purely to stabilise my circulation.
We are standing on a cloud. I have stopped asking questions,
and I recommend you do the same. Questions weigh you down, and on clouds that's dangerous.
The estate agent has sized you up twice from head to toe.
To her you're a property in need of renovation. I hate to contradict her.
Mirror, mirror … oh, it's you. Very nice hair. Very lively. Very brave.
A magnificent tomcat! The build of a lion! The ear: a mark of character!
Thank you, Max! But the princess is in another …
… castle. Your Highness! Found you! I found you!
That's finding with a run-up.
A cat! Come here. No? Fine. Cats that don't come are the honest ones.
Zeldina. Skip the princess, please. I'm looking for a flat, not a rescuer.
Toadi has been looking for me for three years. He's very good at looking and very bad at finding. I've sent him my address three times.
Removal firms are expensive. Dark Lords carry boxes for free.
You get yourself kidnapped, wait to be rescued, and suddenly you live somewhere else. Free of charge.
She wants commission in dragon gold. I have crowns, not dragons. And she won't be talked round. Believe me, I'm up to six months' rent.
I'm here. Between box and clipboard.
Give up. I'm at six.
You just sold my kidnapper to an estate agent.
I'm coming with you. Someone who negotiates like that needs someone who carries things. I've had practice.
Seven floors. Tower location. I heard.
Toadi. I'm standing right here.
You ran after me.
Everyone calls him Mouldword. Not his mother. She had a pet name for him, four parts, dreadful.
All I know is that it starts with "Mo". It's the password to his secret door. He's a very bad Dark Lord.
Live there. Move in. Never move again. Maybe a chandelier. I dream big, but at a fixed price.
Then we'll be flatmates. He sneezes, I tidy up. I've had worse flatmates.
Grimtooth? Been on strike for years. All he really wants is a job with a bunch of keys. A tower would need a caretaker. Just a thought.
You in front. I'll carry.
The last dragon was my landlord. His tower was too expensive. The only thing that kidnapped me was the service charge bill.
He read it. Then he jumped into a pipe to get there faster. Pipes never lead where you want to go.
Long enough that his mother had to take a breath halfway through. In front of his whole class.
I don't mean anything. I'm only dropping hints. They're cheaper than opinions.
A forge. It's about as hot as my phone after three hours of videos in a row.
The embers flicker every time I breathe. I'm breathing sideways now.
An anvil. Heavy, black and quiet. The two of us would have got along great.
I knocked on it, and it sounds like a gong. Somewhere, someone's definitely bowing right now.
Pans, pots, ladles, and every one has a name tag. The name thing must be contagious in this village.
The pan is called "Sizzlebeard", the pot is called "Deepwater". I really don't want to know what the ladle's called.
A white goat with a little bell. She's got a sword in her mouth and she's chewing on it like gum.
The bell jingles when she chews. The smith flinches every time.
The blacksmith. Red beard, soot on his face and the look of a man who no longer loves his goat.
He strokes the goat's head and pulls his hand back really fast. He does still love her, just very carefully.
An empty jug, and there's nothing on its name tag either. I guess the blacksmith wasn't ready yet.
I called into it, and it sounds hollow. The jug's still waiting for its job.
I'll just borrow the jug.
Clong. I hit an anvil. That's enough achievement for one day.
Too hot. My eyebrows vote no.
Why are you forging pans?
Have you ever tried sending her away?
Is the goat yours?
What's that sword in her mouth?
Can I have the goat?
See you.
Why would I milk a goat? I don't even have a reason. Well, not yet.
Okay. Milk. From a goat, with my own hands. I always thought this sort of thing only happened to other people.
Done, a whole jug. I hereby solemnly swear never to milk this goat again. Never, ever again.
No. I swore, and I keep my oaths. Especially the convenient ones.
Goats eat iron, but not fish. Lucky, otherwise Pixel would have one more rival.
You can't milk pans. I didn't actually try, just in my head, but that was enough.
The goat has your swords?
And what if you sold her?
Warm. Very warm. Too warm.
The perfect temperature is exactly two steps to the left. I measured it with my entire body.
Two steps left, I've just measured it again. It remains two.
Science has spoken, young man, and science is now going to lie down there.
She eats iron. I eat tuna. We are both specialists,
but only one of us shows any taste in the matter, and I wouldn't want to embarrass anyone by saying which.
She just winked at me. I shall not wink back, for we are rivals.
What we're competing for, I'm not quite sure. But I shall win, on principle.
Pans that have never been used. A tragedy in tin.
Think of everything one could have fried in them. Fish. More fish. And fish for dessert.
A goat, and she's following us. It took me a whole year to follow your grandfather voluntarily.
She manages it in a second. That's not loyalty, that's sucking up.
She says iron tastes of adventure, and that's why she eats it.
She also says she's never been milked and would like it to stay that way. I promised her nothing.
She swears the same, though with considerably more swear words.
Goatish has a surprising number of them. I learned three new ones and I'm saving them for your grandfather.
The goat chews, the blacksmith sighs. That's the entire programme here,
and there's no other channel. I checked, even behind the forge.
The forge is so lovely and warm. I'd have been asleep long ago,
if you didn't think so loudly. One can hear it all the way over here, and it sounds like dithering.
Take it. Take everything. Just not hope, I don't have any of that left myself.
A cat. Does it eat iron? No? Then it can stay. It can even move in.
Ever since the goat moved in, she eats every blade. She doesn't eat pans. So: pans. That's the market economy.
Three times. She came back every time. With a sword in her mouth. Mine.
The goat belongs to nobody. She just turned up one morning. Like debt.
That was Ingrid. Humbert wanted her for his collection. Now she's goat food. Don't tell him, he gets attached to names.
You want her? Take her! Take her with you! I'll forge you a monument! Out of tin, but a monument!
Go with God. Or with the goat. As long as she goes.
I saw that. I will never forget it. Sadly.
Customers! Pans, pots, ladles. I'm out of swords. Ask the goat.
In her stomach. Don't ask any more, or I'll get sad. I'm close enough already.
